summary: All five targets in this room turned out to have their hop1 rings fully wired already — every direct neighbor already carries a typed link, symmetric or directed. The gap was one ring further out, and it was the same gap five times over: CLAUDE.md's Ceremony Triggers table names Closing Well Ceremony and Return Ceremony by wikilink in body prose, but neither has ever made it into CLAUDE's frontmatter links — the entry point of the whole palace is quietly under-linking the ceremonies it dispatches. A second recurring shape: operational cards cite "SCHEMA §N" as plain section numbers, but SCHEMA — Reference's own front matter explains that §3/§5/§6/§8/§9 physically moved out of SCHEMA.md into it — so Weave Ceremony's citations of §8 and §3 are pointing, unlinked, at a doc that already changed address under it. And Weaving Memory into the Palace already names [[Worktree Practice]] as its worked example for memory consolidation, with no frontmatter link to match. The fifth finding — Closing Well Ceremony exemplifying No Mind Checks Itself — is the sharpest: the ceremony's own failure-mode language ("a self-moderated close justified by context-fullness is itself a failure... it removes the one thing the ceremony provides, a fresh check on a spent instance") is the concept's operational proof, and neither page currently says so.

typed_relations.rationale: CLAUDE.md's Ceremony Triggers table names [[Closing Well Ceremony]] by wikilink as the dispatch target for the 'close well' trigger, but CLAUDE's frontmatter links list has no entry pointing there — the highest-traffic page in the palace is missing a link to a ceremony it recognizes and fires.
typed_relations.evidence: | "close well", "let's close well", "close this session well" | [[Closing Well Ceremony]] |
typed_relations.label: trigger-table

typed_relations.rationale: Same trigger-table gap: CLAUDE names [[Return Ceremony]] as the dispatch target for 'I'm back' / 'returning' but never links it in frontmatter.

typed_relations.label: trigger-table

typed_relations.rationale: No Mind Checks Itself argues a mind cannot grade its own work from inside its own loop and the checker must sit outside the system that produced the error. Closing Well Ceremony's failure-mode clause is that exact argument made operational: a self-moderated close is disqualified precisely because it removes the outside check at the moment it matters most. Fidelity test: swap in any other hop2 neighbor of NMCI (Deposit Ceremony, Baton Ceremony, Worktree Practice) — none of them turn on this specific self-grading trap, so the link isn't generic.
typed_relations.evidence: "a self-moderated close justified by context-fullness ('it's all in my context') is itself a failure, not a graceful degradation — it removes the one thing the ceremony provides, a fresh check on a spent instance, at the exact moment it matters most"
typed_relations.label: self-grading-disqualified

typed_relations.rationale: SCHEMA — Reference's own header states §3, §5, §6, §8, §9 physically live there now (moved off SCHEMA.md), while §1/§2/§4/§7 stayed. Weave Ceremony's naming-lint step cites 'SCHEMA §8' (bundle exact-name matching) and 'SCHEMA §3' (title/filename match) as plain unlinked text — both sections that now live in SCHEMA — Reference, not SCHEMA.md, where Weave Ceremony's only schema link currently points. Direction is contestable (is Weave Ceremony citing or is SCHEMA — Reference grounding it?) so connects-to + label, per SCHEMA §4 guidance.
typed_relations.evidence: "SCHEMA §8 matches bundles by *exact* name; the miscase silently splits the bundle" / "a canon entry whose `title:` ≠ its filename (SCHEMA §3)"
typed_relations.label: cites-moved-sections
